description:
Blade Storm (ground and air F), "the windmill", remade for Sir Bonk's own body. The owner keeps the windmill idea and the tuned storm, but today's clip was made for the old, hunched Bonk and "doesn't fit" him (2026-10-22): on Sir Bonk it spins bent double with his head down (image 3 is today's clip on him; his head sits 0.4 m below its idle height the whole spin).

Who: Sir Bonk is a big, good-hearted wannabe knight in homemade armour: a bucket helm with a broom crest, a tabard with a painted crown, a bedsheet cape, his pot-lid pauldron on his left shoulder, and a plank for a greatsword. He is proud and upright: chest up, head up, looking along the plank. Never hunched, never bent double, never head down.

The move (the owner approved image 1, five poses): he spins on the spot like a hammer thrower, three turns to his LEFT (counter-clockwise seen from above), both hands on the plank's grip, arms nearly straight, the plank held out flat and level at hip height like a windmill's sail. He leans back a little against its pull. The cape streams out behind the turn on its own (the game's spring), so leave the cape chain at rest. Then he ends dizzy: that is the opening.

The game fixes the plank's path, because the plank is the hitbox (three hit windows: ticks 8-28, 29-42 and the finisher 43-58, which change while the plank is behind him). Keep today's path exactly (measured on him): the plank flat and level about 0.6 m above the floor (tip 0.32-0.42 m and hilt about 0.25 m below his idle hips), its tip 2.2-2.4 m from his hips, passing straight behind him at ticks 13, 29, 43 and 59 and straight ahead at 21, 36 and 50: one turn every 14-16 ticks, steady, never stopping. His arms angle down to it from his shoulders: he stays tall and lets the straight arms reach down and out, rather than crouching to the plank.

Feet: the floor is where his soles are in the idle pose. He turns with short, heavy pivot steps, one foot at a time stepping around the other, so his feet stay under his hips; a foot on the floor stays on its spot (it may turn there) without sliding or sinking. His hips stay over the same spot (the game steers him slowly; the clip must not travel).

Beats. Tick 0 is the idle pose: the plank rests on his right shoulder. Ticks 1-5: the left hand comes up and takes the grip beside the right. Ticks 1-9 (pose 1, the coil): feet wide, knees bent, torso twisted hard to his right, both hands swing the plank down off the shoulder until it lies flat behind him at hip height (at tick 9 it points back and to his left), head up. Ticks 9-13: unwind to his left, hips first, then chest, then arms, the plank last; it passes straight behind him at 13. Ticks 13-58: three steady turns with the plank flat at hip height (poses 2 and 3: ahead at 21, behind at 29, ahead at 36, behind at 43), chest up, leaning back against the pull. Ticks 43-58 (pose 4, the finisher): the biggest turn: a slightly lower stance, arms fully out, the back heel lifting, the plank ahead at 50 and behind at 58. Ticks 58-66: the momentum carries him round to a stop with the plank out to his right at tick 66. Ticks 66-86 (pose 5, dizzy): his left hand lets go and goes to the side of his helm, his knees bend inward, the plank droops in his right hand until its tip rests on the floor by tick 76, and his whole body sways in a slow wobble on the spot. Ticks 86-94: he shakes it off and swings the plank back up onto his right shoulder. Ticks 94-100 equal the idle pose.
